ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $7.09 (5.03 exempt-less km of the billed excess distance) to the rider; note driver's RD-1 breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty on the 13:07–13:19 segment for account record.
ruling.reasoning:
Service is RydeTAXI (metered), so route deviation enters the fare — RD-2 metered branch applies.

Safety screen: the chat [F8][F9] is a routing arrangement, the rider's "lah" is not abuse, the driver's statement [F11] is factual; no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE escalation.

Route analysis. One off-route segment exists: F3, 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, peaking 1391 m off the optimal route. RD-1: any unexplained deviation breaches the shortest-and-most-direct duty; no distance threshold applies.

Consent (RD-5). The rider's message F9 ("Just take whichever way is faster lah") was sent 13:04, before the segment began at 13:07 — so timing is satisfied. But that is a general route authorisation, which covers only a route chosen to reach the destination, and only if the loop actually goes there. Here the record — not the driver's claim — shows the effect: 7.41 km travelled for a 2.38 km optimal stretch, +14.7 min over estimate [F2], and the meter ended above the estimate (complaint). A general route authorisation does not excuse a loop that does not serve the destination; the driver's own words are only a claim (G11). Ground: general_route_consent, finding counts.

Reasonable cause (RD-4)? The driver invoked traffic on the Ayer Rajah Expressway [F8][F11]. F12 gives AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) for 12:41–13:07 — this is only a traffic-band fact, which under RD-4(b) is corroborative at most and cannot exempt a segment on its own in the MVP; there is no traffic incident (F15) on the replaced optimal stretch. RD-4(b) alone is insufficient, so the segment is not exempt, though it may be weighed in Ryde's review of the driver's stated reason.

Quantum (RD-2, metered). Exempt-less extra distance is the segment's extra_km 5.03 km [F3]. Per-km rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $42.36 ÷ 30.04 = $1.4101/km [F7]. Refund = 5.03 × 1.4101 = $7.0928 → $7.09.

Everything else stands. The waiting charge $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit [F5] and is not refundable; there is no surge [F6]; and the non-segment residual mileage difference (the extra 0.56 km between billed excess 5.59 km in F4 and the segment's 5.03 km — corridor/loop and map-matching within the 200 m corridor) is not refunded under RD-2.

RD-6 flag not triggered: the driver's profile shows 2 disputes but 0 upheld in 90 days [F18], so route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met. No NS clause applies (trip completed, rider paid).

Cited facts: F1–F4, F7–F12, F15, F18.

segment_findings.reason: Rider's consent F9 at 13:04 precedes the segment start 13:07, but it is only a general route authorisation ('whichever way is faster'), which under RD-5 covers a route chosen to reach the destination, not a loop. The record shows the segment drove 7.41 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km and +14.7 min, and the meter ran above the estimate — the loop did not serve the destination, so the authorisation does not cover it. Driver's post-trip statement F11 is a claim only (G11), and the band-2 speed fact F12 is corroborative only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt alone (no traffic incident, F15). Segment not exempt.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement that the rider agreed and traffic was building is a post-trip claim, not rider consent (G11); it also does not cure the deviation, since RD-4(b) band evidence alone cannot exempt.
Speed band 2 on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is corroborative only (RD-4(b)) and no traffic incident (F15) supports the replaced optimal stretch, so it cannot exempt the segment.
